protocol.core_boundary: Example application only; no change to src, schema, registered-interface protocol or product scheduler.

application.configuration: Exact {'dataset': canonical lower-case hex string}; DEFAULT_DATASET = A*64 + NUL + B*64, COUNTERFACTUAL_DATASET removes only the NUL. Explicit JSON hex transport, JSON-canonical dataset identity shared with common.py.
application.framing: 4-byte RAW1/RLE1/HEX1 magic + uint32 big-endian original length + payload. RAW exact bytes, RLE nonzero count/value pairs, HEX exact lowercase hexadecimal. Strict length, alphabet and complete-payload checks; arbitrary trailing bytes are not silently discarded.
application.metric: len(actual complete container), including the 8-byte header; neither JSON hex output size nor payload-only count.
application.fixed_candidates: baseline RAW; challenger discards NUL before RLE but retains the original declared length; unchecked HEX. Default expected costs 137/12/266, with challenger invalid. Actual no-NUL counterfactual uses the same encoder/decoder/policy rules and challenger becomes valid at 12 bytes.
application.unknown: Unchecked measure validates envelope structure and container-byte cost but does not call the round-trip oracle. Explicit analysis reads all three source FDs through common.read_source_results, verifies captured SHA, recomputes strict decode and exact dataset bytes, and emits a new valid/worse unchecked observation rather than overwriting the original unknown.
application.worker: Actual command [sys.executable, absolute compression.py]; worker imports only stdlib and sibling common. Controller methods import .common. No application-owned runner.
application.finite_scope: Only the declared finite datasets and versioned format are acceptance claims, not universal compression gains or arbitrary workload resource guarantees.

test_scope.independent_oracles: Hand-written RAW/RLE/HEX golden wire bytes and expected decoded bytes. The negative decoder cases do not call the tested encoder to manufacture expected results.
test_scope.actual_worker_boundary: One isolated real supervised stdlib analysis worker consumes three sealed read-only memfds whose envelopes are explicit hand-written unit fixtures. Actual common FD-list and content-SHA checks execute. No SQLite/published-source provenance is claimed for these unit inputs, and this worker is not added to the four full acceptance runs' 16-action accounting.
test_scope.controls: Malformed magic/truncated or wrong lengths, RLE zero/odd/overrun/underrun counts, HEX alphabet/whitespace/case/trailing bytes; default invalid vs changed-input valid; foreign/missing/miscosted source; new valid-but-worse analysis leaves original unknown unchanged; unchecked oracle-call refusal.
test_scope.cleanup: Only this test's captured supervisor handle is waited/stopped, and every created memfd is closed in finally. No host enumeration, bare host signal, provider or GPU.

final_bounded.manifest_and_original_ast_command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import ast,hashlib,json,pathlib
for p in ['examples/acceptance/compression.py','examples/acceptance/common.py','tests/test_acceptance_compression.py','src/orze/core/research_interfaces.py','src/orze/engine/native_cpu_action.py','src/orze/engine/supervised_process.py']:
 raw=pathlib.Path(p).read_bytes(); tree=ast.parse(raw)
 print(json.dumps({'path':p,'sha256':hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),'assert_count':sum(isinstance(n,ast.Assert) for n in ast.walk(tree))}))
old=ast.parse(pathlib.Path('docs/evidence/snapshots/v1-07-before-unchecked-oracle-compression-tests.py').read_bytes())
new=ast.parse(pathlib.Path('tests/test_acceptance_compression.py').read_bytes())
old_asserts=[ast.dump(n,include_attributes=False) for n in ast.walk(old) if isinstance(n,ast.Assert)]
new_asserts=[ast.dump(n,include_attributes=False) for n in ast.walk(new) if isinstance(n,ast.Assert)]
assert all(item in new_asserts for item in old_asserts)
old_functions={n.name:ast.dump(n,include_attributes=False) for n in old.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef)}
new_functions={n.name:ast.dump(n,include_attributes=False) for n in new.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef)}
assert all(new_functions[name]==dump for name,dump in old_functions.items())
print(json.dumps({'all_original_functions_ast_exact':len(old_functions),'original_asserts_preserved':len(old_asserts),'new_asserts':len(new_asserts)}))
PY
